2  THIS MFA FILED U/S. 173(1) OF MV ACT, BY THE ADVOCATE FOR APPELLANT PRAYING THAT THIS HON BLE COURT MAY BE PLEASED TO- ALLOW THE APPEAL,
MODIFY THE IMPUGNED JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED- 27.04.2011 PASED BY THE COURT OF THE MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL NO III, BIJAPUR, IN M.V.C.NO.952/2009 AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION AS PRAYED FOR,
 THE ABOVE MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL HAVING BEEN HEARD ON 07.03.2023 AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT, COMING ON FOR "PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT" THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the MACT- III, Bijapur (henceforth referred as 'Tribunal') in MVC.No.952/2009 dated 27.04.2011.
02.

The records disclose that on 10.03.2009 at about 02.30 p.m. when the deceased Channamma was proceeding as a pedestrian in Sindagi bus stand, at that time the driver of a KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-32/F- 1291 (henceforth referred as 'offending vehicle') came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
As a result, the deceased succumbed at the spot.
03. It is claimed that the deceased was doing coolie work and was earning Rs.05,000/- per month.
The claimants alleged that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.
04. The claim petition was contested by the internal insurer of the offending vehicle.
It contended that the deceased was negligent and due to her negligence the accident occurred.
05. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
06. The husband of the deceased was examined as PW.1 and marked documents as Exs.P.1 to 7.
The respondent - corporation examined one witness as RW.1, but did not mark any document.
07. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal considered awarded the compensation at Rs.4.04,000/-.

08. Insofar as liability to pay the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal noticed the documents placed on record and held that, the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of Channappa @ Channaraddi S/O Sahebgouda ... vs Divisional Controller on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9342085/
2 the offending vehicle and therefore, fastened the liability on the respondents.
09. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and award, the claimants have filed the present appeal.
10. The learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal committed an error in considering the income of the deceased.
He contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced.

He further contended that the Tribunal ought to have been awarded compensation towards loss of consortium at the rate of Rs.40,000/- to each of the claimants as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others, (2018) 18 SCC 130.
11.

sentences.text: The insurer of the offending vehicle on the other hand contended that the deceased was also negligent in the accident and therefore, the Tribunal ought to have proportionately fixed the liability.
12. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.

13. Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be re-determined and re-calculated as under:-
Sl. Awarded by the Enhanced by this Heads No. Tribunal Court 01 Loss of dependency Rs.3,84,000/- Rs.8,96,000/-
(Rs.7,000/- x 12 x 16 x 2/3) 02 Loss of Consortium Rs.0,10,000/- Rs.1,60,000/-
of married life (Rs.40,000x4) 03 Loss of estate Rs.0,05,000/- Rs.00,15,000/- 04 Transportation of Rs.0,05,000/- Rs.00,15,000/-
 dead body and  funeral expenses  Total Rs.4,04,000/- Rs.10,86,000/-
14. In view of the above

, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.952/2009 dated 27.04.2011 is modified.
The compensation of Rs.4,04,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.10,86,000/-.
Channappa @ Channaraddi S/O Sahebgouda ... vs Divisional Controller on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9342085/
3 (c) The respondent - NWKSRTC is liable to pay the enhanced compensation to the claimants along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
(d) The insurer is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(e) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
